applies_why: The text decides a collision in which each side's witnesses are its own chain read together — [CR2]'s Isaiah 7:14 with 8:3, 8:8 and 9:6-7 against [DR3]'s 7:14 with 7:16 and 8:3-4 — the chain-against-chain situation K-C governs.
quote: the sign itself does not state the mechanism
rule_words: the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side
room: The phrase 'never verse by verse' together with 'the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side'. Reading one: the judge's final clause is the retired test — it grounds UNDERDETERMINED on the sign's failure to state the mechanism in its own words, one verse weighed by its silence. Reading two: the clause merely notes that the sign decides nothing by itself, the verdict resting only on the balanced footing of [CR2]'s 8:8 and 9:6-7 answer against [DR3]'s bounds-press. I chose reading one because the judge framed the ground as the verse's non-statement and made it the last stated basis for the verdict instead of weighing the two footings to a result.
why: In a collision K-C orders weighed by footing alone, the judge rested the verdict partly on a single verse's silence — that the sign does not state the mechanism — which is the verse-by-verse stating-verse move the rule retires at a judge's seat for either side.
